# `silk/vector`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Growable owned sequences with allocation-aware mutation, stable sorting, and checked indexing.

## When to use
Use [`Vector`](#Vector) when a sequence must grow or own a runtime-determined number of values. Use a
fixed array when the length is part of the type, and `silk.bytes.Bytes` for bulk byte storage.

## Details
[`make`](#Vector.impl.make) is allocation-free. The first growth reserves four elements and later growth doubles
capacity; [`reserve`](#Vector.impl.reserve) can move that cost ahead of mutation. Growth completes in replacement
storage before committing, so [`append`](#Vector.impl.append) and [`reserve`](#Vector.impl.reserve) leave the vector unchanged on
[`OutOfMemoryError`](./allocator.md#OutOfMemoryError). Removing, clearing, and truncating drop exactly the elements they discard
while retaining capacity.

[`sort`](#Vector.impl.sort) is stable, deterministic, and supports move-only elements, but allocates scratch space.
[`binarySearch`](#Vector.impl.binarySearch) requires an already sorted vector and returns the lowest index among equal
matches.

## Gotchas
[`get`](#Vector.impl.get), [`set`](#Vector.impl.set), and [`remove`](#Vector.impl.remove) trap on an out-of-range index. An [`insert`](#Vector.impl.insert) position must be at
or before the current length. Use [`asSlice`](#Vector.impl.asSlice) to borrow move-only elements because [`get`](#Vector.impl.get)
produces a copied value.

## Examples
### Grow and edit an owned sequence
```silk
import silk.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

import silk.effect { Effect }

import silk.vector { Vector }

effect fn build() -> i32
! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = Vector<i32>.make()
  let first = run Vector<i32>.append(&mut values, 10)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let second = run Vector<i32>.append(&mut values, 30)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let middle = run Vector<i32>.insert(&mut values, 1, 20)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let changed = Vector<i32>.set(&mut values, 2, 22)
  let removed = Vector<i32>.remove(&mut values, 0)
  return Vector<i32>.get(&values, 0) + Vector<i32>.get(&values, 1)
}

effect fn recover(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(build(), recover)
}
```

### Sort values and find the first equal value
```silk
import silk.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

import silk.effect { Effect }

import silk.option { Option }

import silk.usize

import silk.vector { Vector }

effect fn search() -> i32
! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut values = Vector<i32>.make()
  let first = run Vector<i32>.append(&mut values, 3)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let second = run Vector<i32>.append(&mut values, 36)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let third = run Vector<i32>.append(&mut values, 3)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut sorting = Vector<i32>.sort(&mut values)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let sorted = run sorting
  let found = Vector<i32>.binarySearch(&values, 3)
    |> Option<usize>.unwrapOr(99)
  if found != usize.ZERO {
    return 0
  }
  return Vector<i32>.get(&values, 0) + Vector<i32>.get(&values, 1) + Vector<i32>.get(&values, 2)
}

effect fn recover(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(search(), recover)
}
```

<a id="Vector"></a>

## `Vector`

```silk
pub struct Vector<T>
```

Owns an initialized prefix of a growable contiguous allocation.

### Details

The vector releases each initialized element and its storage on drop. Length counts initialized
elements. Capacity counts elements that fit without growth. Borrowed elements retain their
referent lifetimes through replacement, extraction, and required cleanup. An allocation does
not make its payload detached.

<a id="Vector.impl.append"></a>

### Method `append`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn append<'env>(self: &mut Self, value: T) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends one owned value, growing geometrically when capacity is exhausted.

#### Details

The vector takes ownership of `value`. If growth fails, the vector keeps its prior contents,
length, and capacity.

<a id="Vector.impl.insert"></a>

### Method `insert`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn insert<'env>(self: &mut Self, index: usize, value: T) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Inserts one owned value at an index, shifting later elements without requiring T to be Copy.

#### Details

Existing elements from `index` onward move one position to the right. If growth fails, the
vector keeps its prior contents, length, and capacity.

#### Gotchas

`index` must be less than or equal to [`length`](#Vector.impl.length).

<a id="Vector.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get<T: Copy>(self: &Self, index: usize) -> T
```

Copies the element at one index and traps when the index is out of range.

#### When to use

Use this function for a `Copy` element. Use [`asSlice`](#Vector.impl.asSlice) to borrow a move-only element.

```silk
pub fn pop(self: &mut Self) -> Option<T>
```

Removes the last element and returns it. Returns an absent value for an empty vector.

#### Details

<a id="Vector.impl.reserve"></a>

### Method `reserve`

```silk
pub effect fn reserve(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Grows capacity to hold at least `additional` more elements without another allocation.

#### Details

This function does not change the length. If allocation fails, contents, length, and capacity
remain unchanged.

<a id="Vector.impl.reserveExact"></a>

### Method `reserveExact`

```silk
pub effect fn reserveExact(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Reserves space for `additional` elements without geometric capacity growth.

#### When to use

Use when the complete output length is known. Use [`reserve`](#Vector.impl.reserve) for repeated growth.

#### Details

If the current capacity is sufficient, this function does not allocate or shrink storage.
Otherwise, one allocation sets capacity to the current length plus `additional`.
The length stays unchanged. Size overflow or allocation failure leaves all existing state unchanged.

<a id="Vector.impl.sort"></a>

### Method `sort`

```silk
pub effect fn sort<T: Order>(self: &mut Self) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Orders the elements in place. Equal elements keep their input order.

#### Details

The sort is stable and deterministic. It supports move-only elements and allocates scratch
storage. If allocation fails, the vector remains unchanged.

<a id="Vector.impl.binarySearch"></a>

### Method `binarySearch`

```silk
pub fn binarySearch<T: Order>(self: &Self, target: T) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the index of a matching element in a sorted vector, or an absent value when Option.none matches.

#### Details

Returns the lowest matching index when a vector holds several equal elements, so a repeated
search over one vector always answers with the same index.
This function consumes `target` and does not change the vector.

#### Gotchas

The vector must already be ordered by the same `Order` witness.
